title: 2nd Stopping Place 1st Truth Grandeur And Sublimity

questions.question: What is the name of the first truth in the target passage?
questions.answer: It is the truth of grandeur and sublimity.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the first truth?
questions.answer: Allah’s greatness and exalted power show that He has no partner.

questions.question: What distant things are mentioned to show power over the universe?
questions.answer: The stars that are extremely far from one another are mentioned.

questions.question: What living example from the earth is used to show large-scale creation at the same time?
questions.answer: Countless flowers of the same kind spread across the world are mentioned.

questions.question: About how many kinds of plants and animals are said to be managed in spring?
questions.answer: More than two hundred thousand kinds are mentioned.

questions.question: In what short time are these living things cared for and brought forth?
questions.answer: In about five or six weeks.

questions.question: How is this springtime work described in terms of quality?
questions.answer: It is described as orderly, balanced, and free from mix-up, mistake, and flaw.

questions.question: What does spring on earth point people to by way of comparison?
questions.answer: It points to a great bringing-to-life again and reminds people of resurrection.

questions.question: Besides huge cosmic matters, what inner human matter is also said to be known and governed?
questions.answer: Even the hidden thoughts in people’s hearts are known and directed.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from these many acts being treated as one act?
questions.answer: The Doer must be one unique and all-powerful Being.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does this greatness leave no room for?
questions.answer: It leaves no room at all for any partner.

questions.question: What does the passage say grandeur does to the idea of partnership?
questions.answer: It removes that idea completely.

questions.question: Why would giving partners to Allah mean weakness or need?
questions.answer: Because it would suggest His power is not complete by itself.

questions.question: Why would giving partners to Allah also mean imperfection?
questions.answer: Because it would wrongly claim there is some fault, limit, or deficiency in His perfection.

questions.question: What does the passage say a sound mind would think about this claim?
questions.answer: A sound mind would never accept it as possible.

questions.question: Why is assigning partners described as a very serious sin?
questions.answer: Because it is an offense against Allah’s glory, greatness, and majesty.

questions.question: What does the quoted Qur’anic warning say about this sin compared with other sins?
questions.answer: It says this sin is not forgiven, while lesser sins may be forgiven.

questions.question: What is the title of the second truth?
questions.answer: It is the absoluteness, comprehensiveness, and open appearance of the Lordly acts in the universe.

questions.question: What is said to limit and direct these acts?
questions.answer: Allah’s wisdom and will, along with the capacities of the things and places where the acts appear.

questions.question: Which false explanations are rejected as real causes of these works?
questions.answer: Chance, nature, blind force, unconscious causation, and scattered elements are rejected.

questions.question: If those things are not real causes, what role do they have?
questions.answer: They are only outward means or coverings used by Allah’s command, will, and power.

questions.question: How many examples does the passage say will be given for the second truth?
questions.answer: Three examples.

questions.question: From which surah are those three examples said to come?
questions.answer: They are said to come from Surah al-Nahl.

questions.question: Which truth comes first in the target passage?
questions.answer: The first truth is grandeur and sublimity.

questions.question: What overall lesson does this first truth teach about Allah?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah’s greatness and majesty prove His oneness.

questions.question: How does the passage show that one Being controls the farthest parts of creation?
questions.answer: It says the same Being creates and manages stars that are vastly separated.

questions.question: How does the passage show that one Being controls similar living things across the earth?
questions.answer: It says the same kind of flowers are created at the same time all over the world.

questions.question: What season is presented as a major sign of Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Spring is presented as a major sign.

questions.question: Why is spring such an important sign in the passage?
questions.answer: Because huge numbers of living things are brought out in a short time with order and balance.

questions.question: What numbers are given to make the spring example stronger?
questions.answer: More than two hundred thousand kinds and more than a hundred thousand examples are mentioned.

questions.question: What does the passage say about mistakes or confusion in this work?
questions.answer: It says there is no confusion, defect, or error in it.

questions.question: What movement of the earth is mentioned as part of Allah’s control?
questions.answer: The earth’s turning and the change between night and day are mentioned.

questions.question: How wide is Allah’s knowledge, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It reaches from the huge universe down to the secret thoughts of people’s hearts.

questions.question: Why does the passage call all these many works really one act?
questions.answer: Because they come from one single Doer with one will and power.

questions.question: What does that teach about the One who does them?
questions.answer: That He is unique, powerful, and without any partner.

questions.question: How does the passage connect partnership with limiting Allah?
questions.answer: It says partnership would wrongly place limits on His all-reaching greatness and perfection.

questions.question: According to the passage, what would partnership wrongly suggest about Allah’s perfection?
questions.answer: It would wrongly suggest defect or incompleteness.

questions.question: What kind of mind is specifically said to reject this idea?
questions.answer: A sound and healthy intellect rejects it.

questions.question: Why is shirk described as deeply serious in this section?
questions.answer: Because it insults Allah’s grandeur, glory, and exalted rank.

questions.question: What Qur’anic ruling is mentioned about shirk?
questions.answer: That Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, though He may forgive lesser sins.

questions.question: What is emphasized at the start of the second truth?
questions.answer: The full, wide-reaching, and clearly seen Lordly actions in the universe.

questions.question: What keeps these actions from being random or uncontrolled?
questions.answer: Allah’s wisdom and will keep them measured and directed.

questions.question: What does the passage say about chance and blind forces in relation to creation?
questions.answer: They have no share in these wise, balanced, life-giving works.

questions.question: Why are natural causes described as only a veil?
questions.answer: Because they hide the direct working of Allah’s power from plain sight.

questions.question: How many examples are promised to explain this second truth?
questions.answer: Three examples are promised.

questions.question: What is the first truth called in this passage?
questions.answer: It is called the truth of grandeur and sublimity.

questions.question: What does “sublimity” point to in this passage?
questions.answer: It points to Allah’s supreme majesty and exalted greatness.

questions.question: Which two very different scales of creation are brought together to show Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Very distant stars and the hidden thoughts inside human hearts.

questions.question: What does the passage say about flowers of one species across the globe?
questions.answer: They are brought into existence in the same manner and at the same time across different regions.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to many plants and animals during spring?
questions.answer: They are managed, fed, revived, distinguished, and beautified with great order.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the result of this spring work?
questions.answer: It describes it as regular, balanced, and free of confusion.

questions.question: Why is spring compared to resurrection?
questions.answer: Because life returns on a massive scale, showing a sign of being raised again.

questions.question: What earlier great event does the passage say spring helps prove to people?
questions.answer: It helps point to the creation of the heavens and the earth.

questions.question: What daily sign in the world is mentioned along with this?
questions.answer: The changing and interweaving of night and day.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah’s knowledge of people?
questions.answer: He knows even the most hidden and quiet thoughts within hearts.

questions.question: What is the logical conclusion after listing these works?
questions.answer: The One doing them must be single, mighty, and unmatched.

questions.question: According to the passage, how much room is left for a partner in these works?
questions.answer: No room at all is left.

questions.question: What four wrong ideas would partnership imply about Allah in this section?
questions.answer: It would imply weakness, need, fault, and limitation.

questions.question: Why is limiting Allah especially wrong in this passage’s argument?
questions.answer: Because His greatness and perfection are described as all-encompassing.

questions.question: What kind of person would refuse to believe such a false idea?
questions.answer: Anyone with sound understanding would refuse it.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the seriousness of shirk?
questions.answer: It describes it as a grave crime against Allah’s majesty.

questions.question: Which Divine qualities are especially said to be offended by shirk here?
questions.answer: His grandeur, the dignity of His glory, and His sublimity.

questions.question: What is the central theme of the second truth?
questions.answer: The Lordly acts in the universe are absolute, wide-reaching, and openly visible everywhere.

questions.question: What two things does the passage say set the limits for those acts?
questions.answer: Allah’s wisdom and will, and the capacities of created things and places.

questions.question: What features of these deeds prove they do not come from random causes?
questions.answer: Their balance, wisdom, insight, life-giving nature, order, and firmness.

questions.question: Name two of the false causes the passage rejects.
questions.answer: It rejects chance and blind force.

questions.question: If those causes are not true makers, how are they described instead?
questions.answer: They are described as outward coverings or means used under Allah’s command.

questions.question: What does the passage say is coming next to explain the second truth?
questions.answer: Three examples from connected verses in Surah al-Nahl.

questions.question: What subject is discussed first in the marked passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s grandeur and sublimity are discussed first.

questions.question: What does the passage try to prove through this first truth?
questions.answer: It tries to prove that Allah is one and cannot have partners.

questions.question: What example from space is used to show control over vast distances?
questions.answer: The creation and management of stars far apart from each other.

questions.question: What example from plant life is used to show unity in creation on earth?
questions.answer: The creation of countless flowers of the same kind all over the earth.

questions.question: What large number of living kinds is mentioned in connection with spring?
questions.answer: More than two hundred thousand kinds of plants and animals.

questions.question: What is said about the timing of this spring activity?
questions.answer: It happens in only five or six weeks.

questions.question: What qualities mark this activity?
questions.answer: It is marked by regularity, balance, and freedom from mistake.

questions.question: What does this spring display give people a sample of?
questions.answer: It gives a sample of a great rising to life again.

questions.question: What repeating pattern in time is mentioned as another sign of rule and control?
questions.answer: The passing of night into day and day into night.

questions.question: How close does Divine knowledge come to human beings in this passage?
questions.answer: It reaches even the secret thoughts hidden in their hearts.

questions.question: When many different works are called one act, what does that show?
questions.answer: It shows they come from one single Actor.

questions.question: How does the passage describe that Actor?
questions.answer: As unique, powerful, glorious, and majestic.

questions.question: What happens to the idea of shirk in the face of such greatness?
questions.answer: It is completely rejected and uprooted.

questions.question: Why would accepting a partner be an insult to Divine power?
questions.answer: Because it would make it seem needy or unable to act fully on its own.

questions.question: Why would accepting a partner be an insult to Divine perfection?
questions.answer: Because it would suggest an imperfection or defect.

questions.question: Why would accepting a partner be an insult to Divine vastness?
questions.answer: Because it would place a boundary on what is without limit.

questions.question: How does the passage appeal to reason here?
questions.answer: It says no sound intellect can accept such a claim.

questions.question: How does the Qur’anic warning strengthen the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that associating partners with Allah is treated as the gravest kind of wrong.

questions.question: What is highlighted in the second truth about Allah’s actions in the universe?
questions.answer: Their unlimited scope, all-including reach, and clear appearance.

questions.question: What controls these actions so they are not chaotic?
questions.answer: Allah’s wisdom and will control them.

questions.question: What else affects how these actions appear in the world?
questions.answer: The built-in abilities of the things and places where they appear.

questions.question: Why can’t chance or nature be the true source of these actions?
questions.answer: Because the actions are wise, balanced, life-giving, and orderly, not random or blind.

questions.question: According to the passage, what purpose do such natural causes serve?
questions.answer: They serve only as outward veils covering Allah’s direct power.

questions.question: How many examples are announced before the passage stops?
questions.answer: Three examples are announced.

questions.question: What is the heading of the first truth in the marked section?
questions.answer: It is grandeur and sublimity.

questions.question: In simple terms, what does this truth teach?
questions.answer: Allah’s greatness is so complete that no partner can be joined with Him.

questions.question: What does the passage emphasize about the way this spring work is done?
questions.answer: It is done with precision, balance, and no disorder.

questions.question: Why is this spring work important for belief in resurrection?
questions.answer: Because it gives a visible example of life returning after death-like stillness.

questions.question: What verse-related event from early creation is spring said to help prove?
questions.answer: The creation of the heavens and the earth.

questions.question: Which everyday cycle is used as another sign of Divine control?
questions.answer: The changing of night and day.

questions.question: What hidden human reality is included under Allah’s knowledge and management?
questions.answer: People’s inner thoughts and quiet feelings.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying each of these deeds is really one deed?
questions.answer: It means they all come from the same single source.

questions.question: What does that single source have to be like?
questions.answer: It has to be one unique and mighty Being.

questions.question: Does the passage allow even a small possibility of partners?
questions.answer: No, it says there is not even the slightest opening for that.

questions.question: What four problems would follow if partners were assigned to Allah?
questions.answer: It would imply weakness, need, flaw, and limitation.

questions.question: Why is limitation especially impossible according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because Allah’s greatness and perfection embrace everything.

questions.question: What role does human reason play in this argument?
questions.answer: Right reason recognizes that such partnership is impossible.

questions.question: How is shirk judged morally in this section?
questions.answer: It is judged to be an extremely serious offense.

questions.question: Why is shirk such a serious offense here?
questions.answer: Because it dishonors Allah’s majesty, glory, and exalted greatness.

questions.question: What does the second truth focus on?
questions.answer: It focuses on the Lordly acts spread throughout the universe.

questions.question: How are these acts described in range and visibility?
questions.answer: They are described as unlimited, all-encompassing, and openly appearing.

questions.question: What gives these acts their measure and boundaries?
questions.answer: Allah’s wisdom and will give them measure, along with the capacities of created things.

questions.question: What mistaken explanations are pushed aside?
questions.answer: Random luck, nature, blind power, unconscious causes, and scattered elements.

questions.question: Why are those explanations rejected?
questions.answer: Because they cannot produce works that are so wise, balanced, and full of life.

questions.question: If they are not true causes, what are they in relation to Allah’s work?
questions.answer: They are only outward coverings or tools under His command.

questions.question: What does the passage say will be used to explain this second truth further?
questions.answer: Three examples connected with three verses in Surah al-Nahl.

questions.question: What is the very first truth named in the target passage?
questions.answer: The first truth is grandeur and sublimity.

questions.question: What belief does this truth support?
questions.answer: It supports belief in Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What example from the sky shows Allah’s power over enormous scale?
questions.answer: The stars, even though they are separated by huge distances.

questions.question: What example from the earth shows Allah’s power over many matching creations?
questions.answer: The many flowers of the same type spread across the world.

questions.question: How many kinds of plant and animal life are mentioned as being handled together?
questions.answer: More than two hundred thousand kinds.

questions.question: What short time period is given for this organized work?
questions.answer: Five or six weeks.

questions.question: Which qualities of this work argue against confusion?
questions.answer: Its regularity, balance, and freedom from error argue against confusion.

questions.question: What major belief is strengthened by the yearly return of life in spring?
questions.answer: Belief in resurrection is strengthened.

questions.question: What ongoing event involving day and night is mentioned?
questions.answer: Night enters day and day enters night.

questions.question: How far does Allah’s administration extend according to this passage?
questions.answer: It extends from the farthest cosmic events to the deepest private thoughts of people.

questions.question: Why does the passage say all these are truly one act?
questions.answer: Because one will and one power carry them out together.

questions.question: What does that say about the Doer?
questions.answer: The Doer is one, powerful, and beyond all partnership.

questions.question: What effect does Divine grandeur have on the idea of sharing rule?
questions.answer: It completely blocks and removes that idea.

questions.question: What wrong view of Allah’s power would partnership create?
questions.answer: It would make His power seem needy or incomplete.

questions.question: What wrong view of Allah’s greatness would partnership create?
questions.answer: It would make His greatness seem flawed.

questions.question: What wrong view of Allah’s perfection would partnership create?
questions.answer: It would suggest imperfection where there is complete perfection.

questions.question: What wrong view of Allah’s all-embracing nature would partnership create?
questions.answer: It would suggest limits where there are no limits.

questions.question: What does the passage say about a healthy intellect and this issue?
questions.answer: A healthy intellect would not accept partnership as possible.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the sin of associating partners with Allah?
questions.answer: It describes it as an extremely grave crime.

questions.question: What is the reason given for the gravity of this sin?
questions.answer: It offends Allah’s grandeur, glorious dignity, and sublimity.

questions.question: What is the subject of the second truth?
questions.answer: It is the absolute and all-encompassing nature of the Lordly acts in the universe.

questions.question: What limits these acts so they appear in fitting ways?
questions.answer: Allah’s wisdom and will, and the abilities of created things, limit them fittingly.

questions.question: Why can’t blind causes explain these acts?
questions.answer: Because the acts are wise, measured, life-giving, and firmly ordered.

questions.question: What examples of false causes are named?
questions.answer: Chance, nature, blind force, unconscious causality, and the elements.

questions.question: What place do those things have if they are not true makers?
questions.answer: They are only apparent veils used by Allah’s command, will, and power.

questions.question: How many examples are about to be presented after this introduction?
questions.answer: Three examples are about to be presented.
